records.supported_name_scope: Río Aguanaval is directly supported for the long central river corridor and its drainage context. The selected object also includes the San Francisco and Leobardo Reynoso headwater/reservoir setting, a lower connector cartographically distinguished as canal, and an eastern continuation into the La Barranca/Viesca drainage setting. The evidence supports this composite route but does not establish Aguanaval as one representative hydronym covering the entire selected object. No composite name is proposed as an official name.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The complete single fragment was inspected from its western headwater approach, through the southern reservoir bend and long northward Zacatecas reach, the eastward bulge and northwestward middle course, the lower northward bend, and the east/southeast terminal continuation. Original INEGI state and municipal maps distinguish this Aguanaval-centered route from the Nazas–Mayrán corridor farther north and west. The retained Durango source was re-read for this object; the earlier Nazas object's identity was not transferred.
records.region: Central-northern Mexico: western Fresnillo and Río Grande in Zacatecas, the eastern Durango and southwestern Coahuila river corridor, and the southern Laguna plain toward Viesca.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded whole-route correspondence and naming-scope hold using readable original official pixels. Further acquisition is not pending for this assessment. A future whole-object or representative-system assignment would require positive evidence encompassing the separately named upper approach and the canal/receiving-channel/terminal continuation, rather than extending the central river label by inference. Exact hydronym transitions and present flow remain unassigned.

naming_scope_details.upper_corridor: San Francisco drainage and Presa Gobernador Leobardo Reynoso (Trujillo), followed by the Aguanaval approach. The starting feeder and exact transitions remain unassigned.
naming_scope_details.middle_corridor: The named Aguanaval through Zacatecas, eastern Durango and southwestern Coahuila; Santiago–Santa Clara is a separate joining route.
naming_scope_details.lower_connector: A short northward connection is mapped as canal. Its exact engineering name, operation and hydraulic continuity are not established.
naming_scope_details.receiving_and_terminal_scope: Eastern La Barranca/Viesca drainage setting with multiple channels and a terminal-basin context. La Barranca is retained as a separate mapped name in that setting, not asserted for every selected lower vertex. Laguna de Viesca is basin context, not a blanket river alias or verified contemporary water surface.
naming_scope_details.excluded_name_transfer: Nazas, Mayrán, Arroyo de Cuencamé, Santiago–Santa Clara, nearby settlement names and reservoir labels are not substituted for unsupported parts of the selected object.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: One display fragment and modeled-mainstem membership do not establish one natural river, one hydronym, a natural source-to-mouth length, current permanence or operating canal connectivity. The hold does not imply that unresolved sections are unnamed. Formal aliases and Korean translation remain unassigned.
naming_scope_details.completion_scope: Completed bounded whole-route correspondence and naming-scope hold using readable original official pixels. Further acquisition is not pending for this assessment. A future whole-object or representative-system assignment would require positive evidence encompassing the separately named upper approach and the canal/receiving-channel/terminal continuation, rather than extending the central river label by inference. Exact hydronym transitions and present flow remain unassigned.

records.supported_name_scope: Hamlin Valley Wash is directly documented as a local drainage in the southern valley, but an exact selected-channel extent is not established. Named Snake Valley streams, desert drainage, evaporation-basin context and the terminal Great Salt Lake passage remain distinct. No local stream name is promoted to the complete object.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The entire three-piece route was read, including its southern eastward hook, Nevada-side northward leg, Snake Valley passage, northeastward approach to the desert, long desert bends and final western Great Salt Lake continuation. It does not follow the Utah–Wyoming–Idaho Bear River corridor or the Sevier River.
records.region: Western Utah and adjoining eastern Nevada, United States; inland Great Basin, from Hamlin Valley north through Snake Valley and the Great Salt Lake Desert toward western Gunnison Bay.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded correspondence and naming-scope hold. Independent readable official maps cover the regional route, Snake Valley stream context and terminal lake. No further source acquisition is pending. Follow-up is required only before any future assignment or subdivision of names.

naming_scope_details.local_name_context: Hamlin Valley Wash is a documented local drainage, not a supported whole-object candidate. Exact correspondence to individual selected vertices remains unassigned.
naming_scope_details.unassigned: Initial feeder, local wash/channel transitions, intervening valley-floor and playa paths, precise river-to-playa or lake boundaries, and the modeled terminal line as a named linear feature.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Three modeled mainstem pieces and their aggregate length do not demonstrate a single natural river, a perennial surface connection, present pond or lake inundation, or an official source-to-mouth length. The hold does not mean every local portion is unnamed. No Korean form, historical alias sequence or naming date was established.

records.supported_name_scope: No natural river identity is established for the complete modeled Inland Ice path. This completed feature-class and naming-scope hold does not claim that every nearby marginal stream is unnamed.
records.geographic_disambiguation: East-central Greenland Inland Ice and its eastern ice-margin setting inland of the Scoresby Sund region. Nearby land, glacier and fjord labels provide regional context only; no exact terminal natural feature is assigned.
records.completion_scope: Readable coverage supports the completed scope hold. Positive natural-river identity evidence would be required before any later name assignment; no further acquisition is pending now.

naming_scope_details.length_limit: Model display length, not a measured natural-river length.

records.supported_name_scope: Rivière Harricana identifies the connecting river trunk from the Val-d’Or lake setting through Amos and north toward James Bay. Rivière Turgeon identifies the separate western contribution. Headward feeder, lake and coastal transition scopes remain distinct, without assigning exact hydronym boundary vertices.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The whole selected route was inspected: its southeastern headward curve, connected lakes, passage through Amos, long north-northwest trunk, west-side Turgeon contribution and final crossing toward the James Bay coast jointly match the Harricana system. Abitibi here describes the regional setting; the Abitibi River drainage farther west is distinct.
records.region: Abitibi-Témiscamingue and Nord-du-Québec, continuing across the Ontario boundary toward southern James Bay, Canada.
records.completion_scope: Completed for bounded representative-system correspondence using original CEHQ and OBVAJ maps and supporting provincial conservation-plan prose. Exact feeder-to-lake, lake-to-river and river-to-estuary transitions remain unassigned. The old conservation-plan map-enlargement link returned a relocation page and supplied no readable enlarged map; it was not necessary for the final determination.

naming_scope_details.geographic_qualifier: Abitibi–James Bay describes the corridor and is an editorial qualifier, not part of the official hydronym.
naming_scope_details.upper_scope: Selected Senneville–Blouin headward approach and westward connection into the Harricana corridor. No continuous official Harricana name is assigned to the initial feeder or to the lakes.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: Three selected pieces represent the lower Turgeon approach. The mapped Wawagosic, Théo, Plamondon, Samson and other branches provide context but are not additional selected contributions or Harricana aliases.
naming_scope_details.lake_scope: Senneville and Blouin belong to the selected southern approach; Malartic, La Motte, Figuery and Obalski occur along the northward corridor. The separately contributing Mourier–Lemoine–De Montigny chain is not substituted for the actual modeled headward route. Lake names are not promoted to river aliases, and exact shoreline transitions remain unassigned.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Lower Harricana crossing toward the Ontario side of southern James Bay. The regional map and provincial prose support the coastal destination; they do not establish an exact endpoint relationship to a surveyed mouth or tidal limit.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Modeled mainstem status and selected fragment boundaries do not establish official hydronym boundaries. Rendered model length is not an official natural-river length. No naming date, Indigenous-name equivalence, historical alias sequence or Korean form was established.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Keep the saved order unchanged and use later result IDs/status changes to mark progress. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated; no lake research until all river continental phases have had their review pass.
